chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who finds in his head pain from a severe headache, is it permissible for him to break [the fast]?

He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he suffers a severe headache, and when he has a severe fever, and when his eyes are sore with severe soreness, then it has become permissible for him to break [the fast].'
ai.seo_question: What specific illnesses allow a Muslim to break their fast during Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the threshold of 'severe' distress (shadid) required to exempt a fasting person from obligatory prayer, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that hardship removes obligation (al-mashaqqah tajlib al-taysir). It specifically validates breaking the fast for intense cephalalgia, high fever, and severe ocular inflammation, ensuring that the physical burden does not become unbearable. This ruling underscores the balance between spiritual discipline and physiological preservation in Islamic law.
